title: Factitious cheilitis: a case report
case_prompt: A 56-year-old woman presented with a 4-year history of a slowly enlarging lesion on her lower lip. She had no significant medical history, was a non-smoker, and denied weight loss. On examination, there was a painless, firm, indurated, crusted area measuring 4 cm with central ulceration, giving the lip a “bitten-off” appearance. The surrounding skin and oral mucosa were normal. There were no palpable lymph nodes, and ultrasonography confirmed the absence of lymphadenopathy. Complete blood count, erythrocyte sedimentation rate, and routine serum chemistries were all within normal limits. An incisional biopsy including normal mucosa and skin showed a non-specific ulcer with inflammation and granulation tissue and revealed no cellular atypia suggestive of malignancy.
diagnostic_reasoning:
1. Malignancy was considered for a chronic ulcerative lesion but was excluded because “There was no cellular atypia in favor of malignancy.”  
2. Infectious cheilitis was considered but deemed unlikely as “Cultures and histopathologic examination are prudent to rule out … specific infectious etiology.”  
3. Actinic cheilitis was considered since sun damage can lead to similar lesions: “Actinic cheilitis … should be considered in the differential diagnosis of crusted and ulcerated lesions of the lip.”  
4. Contact dermatitis was considered due to possible irritant or allergic causes: “Contact dermatitis … should be considered in the differential diagnosis of crusted and ulcerated lesions of the lip.”  
5. Photosensitivity reactions were considered because light-induced dermatitis may affect the lip: “Photosensitivity reactions … should be considered in the differential diagnosis of crusted and ulcerated lesions of the lip.”  
6. Neoplasia was included among malignancies mimicking this appearance: “… neoplasia that may look similar on physical exam.”  
7. Exfoliative cheilitis was considered as a compulsive self-injury disorder: “We noticed that there is an interchangeable usage of exfoliative cheilitis and factitious cheilitis in the literature.”  
8. Cheilitis glandularis was considered for glandular inflammation presenting with crusting: “… cheilitis glandularis … that may look similar on physical exam.”  
9. Hypervitaminosis A was considered because vitamin A excess can cause cheilitis: “Also hypervitaminosis A … have to be ruled out.”  
10. Lupus erythematosus was considered as an autoimmune cause of lip lesions: “Also lupus erythematosus … have to be ruled out.”  
11. Lichenoid dermatosis was considered since immune-mediated rash can involve the lip: “Also … lichenoid dermatosis have to be ruled out.”  
12. Thyroid abnormality was evaluated because of reported associations, but thyroid function tests were normal: “Some data suggests an associated thyroid abnormality … In our patient thyroid function tests were normal.”
